definitions.explanation: The basic verb for dying, used of people and animals. Plants wither rather than die: 枯れる is the normal verb for them. When speaking about people, 亡くなる is usually preferred as the gentler, more respectful word.

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{犬|いぬ}→犬：00632_inu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{去年|きょねん}→去年：00727_kyonen⟧{死|し}にました。
⟦{虫|むし}→虫：02262_mushi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{死|し}んでいる。

examples.english: My grandfather died ten years ago.
examples.notes: In more polite speech, ⟦亡くなりました→亡くなる：02639_nakunaru⟧ would be used

examples.japanese: ⟦{魚|さかな}→魚：00499_sakana⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦あげない→あげる：00546_ageru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{死|し}んでしまいます⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: If you don't give water to the fish, it will die.

examples.japanese: ⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{飼|か}っていた→飼う：08151_kau⟧⟦{猫|ねこ}→猫：02237_neko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{先月|せんげつ}→先月：00751_sengetsu⟧{死|し}んで、⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧⟦{悲|かな}しい→悲しい：00783_kanashii⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
examples.english: The cat I was keeping died last month, and I'm very sad.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: ⟦{自動詞|じどうし}→自動詞：10977_jidoushi⟧ (intransitive). No pair verb. Pattern: X⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{死|し}ぬ (X dies).

ASPECT: ている indicates resulting state. {死|し}んでいる = 'is dead' (state, not process of dying).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ⟦{病気|びょうき}→病気：00771_byouki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{死|し}ぬ (die of illness)
- ⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{死|し}ぬ (die in an accident)
- {死|し}にそう (about to die - also used hyperbolically)
- {死|し}んでしまった (has died - regret)
- {死|し}ぬ⟦ほど→程：01724_hodo⟧〜 (〜 to death: {死|し}ぬほど⟦{疲|つか}れた→疲れる：00901_tsukareru⟧, dead tired)

CONJUGATION:
{死|し}ぬ is the only ぬ-ending godan verb in everyday use. Its て/た forms take ん: {死|し}んで, {死|し}んだ (not {死|し}にて/{死|し}にた).

WHICH VERB FOR WHAT DIES:
- {死|し}ぬ: people and animals
- ⟦{枯|か}れる→枯れる：04589_kareru⟧: plants (wither, dry up) — {花|はな}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{死|し}ぬ sounds wrong
- ⟦{亡|な}くなる→亡くなる：02639_nakunaru⟧: people only, and the polite default when talking about someone's death

REGISTER:
Said of a person, {死|し}ぬ is blunt and factual. Use it for statistics, news, and one's own hypotheticals; switch to ⟦{亡|な}くなる→亡くなる：02639_nakunaru⟧ when speaking of someone's family or in any careful conversation.
